notes: 39/39 tests, 69/69 assertions, port:parity --complete clean. All five jsdom stubs deleted. GAINED is the thesis: real layout + real ResizeObserver cover shared/useSize.ts L19-48, SliderThumbImpl.vue L40 (getThumbInBoundsOffset only runs once the thumb has a measured size) and Slider/utils.ts L67-70,L110-111. The single LOST line is itself a finding — see #linear-scale-degenerate. Two structural deviations, both recorded below: #form-submit-button and #home-end-name.

QUARANTINED via it.fails — reported, not fixed. The jsdom axe test is vacuous: Slider.test.ts:27-33 calls axe(wrapper.element) synchronously after mount(), before Vue flushes, so the thumb still carries display:none from SliderThumbImpl.vue:80 (the SSR anti-jank branch, active while value === undefined). axe skips hidden elements, so aria-input-field-name comes back INAPPLICABLE and the only interactive element in the component is never audited. await render() flushes, axe sees the thumb, and reports a real violation: single-thumb sliders have no accessible name because getLabel (utils.ts:35) only auto-labels 2+ thumbs and the story fixture supplies none. The gap is in the fixture, not the library. Not strictly a jsdom-vs-browser difference — jsdom reports it too once flushed (verified experimentally) — but browser mode is what surfaced it. Resolve by giving _Slider.vue an aria-label, NOT by disabling the rule.

The only line the browser port fails to cover is Slider/utils.ts:109 — linearScale's `if (input[0] === input[1]) return output[0]` short-circuit. jsdom takes that branch on EVERY pointer test, because the slider measures 0x0 so `rect.width - thumbWidth` is 0; the browser takes L110-111, the real interpolation, instead. So a line the jsdom suite reports as covered was only ever covered by the absence of layout, and the arithmetic the component actually ships was never executed. This is the coverage-parity oracle's first justified LOST line; exempted via PORT-COVERAGE-ALLOW.tsv, which is machine-checked against this file. Generalises: coverage lost to a port is not automatically a regression, but it must be argued line by line.

The jsdom form block fires a synthetic `submit` on the <form>, which no user can do. Ported with a real <button type="submit"> (see AGENTS.md 'Settled questions' — implicit submission via Enter on the focused thumb does NOT submit this form, 0 calls, and neither suite would have caught that). Also: vitest-browser-vue unmounts after every test, so the component is rendered per test in a beforeEach rather than once at describe-body level as the original does. The module-level handleSubmit spy still accumulates calls across tests, so the original's 1-then-2 call-count assertions port unchanged.

Naming bug in the jsdom original, carried over verbatim: under 'when vertical > when inverted', `it('home should set value to 100')` asserts 0 and `it('end should set value to 0')` asserts 100. The assertions are right — Home/End are semantic (min/max) per ARIA APG and ignore `inverted` by design — and the names are simply wrong. PORTING.md rule 4 says to fix the test so the name becomes true, but applying it here would fail a component that is behaving correctly, so the assertions were kept and the deviation recorded here. Browser mode contributed nothing to finding this; reading the file did.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (PORTING.md 2.3), the T3 thesis proved rather than asserted. Deleting `target.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)` from SliderImpl.vue's pointerdown handler — i.e. breaking pointer capture outright — makes the browser port's 'should emit valueCommit on wrapper' FAIL and leaves the jsdom test PASSING. jsdom passes because its own mock, `hasPointerCapture: vi.fn().mockImplementation(id => id)`, answers yes for a capture that was never taken, so pointerup still emits slideEnd. The jsdom test cannot fail this mutation by construction. Source reverted immediately; verified with git diff.

PORTED, 10/10 tests and 18/18 assertions; port:parity --complete and port:checklist --complete both clean; coverage loses nothing. VERDICT REVISED — this row previously read `stay-jsdom` and recommended skipping the other 12 T1 files. GENERALISES TO ALL 97 FILES, AND IS A TRAP IN THE ORACLE. The one line the browser port covers and jsdom does not is useForwardExpose.ts:68 — the `if (!ref) return` detach path, which Vue runs only when a template ref is released at unmount. Chromium has nothing to do with it: vitest-browser-vue registers beforeEach(cleanup), and cleanup() calls wrapper.unmount() (dist/index.js + dist/pure-*.js), so every ported test tears its component down, whereas the jsdom original mounts 10 times and never unmounts once. Verified, not assumed: a throwaway jsdom test doing mount() then wrapper.unmount() covers L68 with istanbul hit count 1 (probe written, measured, deleted). Two lessons. (1) A coverage GAIN from port:coverage is not automatically evidence for browser mode — check whether the harness or the environment earned it, or the thesis gets credited with wins it did not achieve. (2) The more useful direction: reka-ui jsdom suite exercises almost no component teardown, and porting picks that up for free.

AUDIT OF THE OTHER 12 T1 FILES. CONCLUSION REVISED — this row previously concluded `stay-jsdom` for all 12. Under the delete-jsdom goal the split is different: 4 of the 12 need no DOM at all and have MOVED TO THE `node` PROJECT (date/calendar, shared/color/gradient, shared/color/utils, shared/useSingleOrMultipleValue), and the remaining 8 are DOM-dependent and are queued for browser mode (component/Arrow, getActiveElement, useArrowNavigation, useComposing, useForwardProps, useForwardScopeId, useIsUsingKeyboard, useSelectionBehavior). THE EVIDENCE THE AUDIT PRODUCED IS UNCHANGED AND STILL WORTH HAVING, because it says these 8 ports should be expected to be boring rather than revealing: each of the 4 non-pure files was checked against the specific way its jsdom test could be green for the wrong reason, and all 4 came back negative. The notable one is getActiveElement, an expected WIN that was not one — the function is nothing but a shadow-DOM retargeting loop, so a jsdom that failed to retarget would make that loop dead code (the Slider-axe failure mode). THE T2 TRIAL RUN (PORTING.md phase 1). 7/7 tests, 7/7 assertions, port:parity --complete and port:checklist --complete clean, coverage gains 1 line and loses none. Mechanically the easiest port so far and still worth three further findings, which is the argument for running T2 as real ports rather than assuming they are rubber-stamps. Two translation gaps the table did not cover, both now added to AGENTS.md. (1) The original uses @testing-library/vue render, not VTU mount, and asserts on .html() four times; vitest-browser-vue exposes no VTU wrapper and therefore no .html() at all (its render returns container / locator / emitted / rerender / unmount and the locator selectors). @testing-library/vue's is literally "html: () => wrapper.html()" (dist/render.js:53), i.e. the component root's outerHTML, so container.firstElementChild.outerHTML is the exact translation and all four expected strings port unchanged. A locator assertion is NOT a substitute here: the original pins the ENTIRE rendered output, and toHaveAttribute would check one attribute and let extra ones through. (2) The original's beforeEach clearing document.body.innerHTML is deleted outright — render unmounts and removes its container after every test. AXE IS NOT VACUOUS HERE, unlike Slider's: probed the result object, 5 rules pass (label, form-field-multiple-labels, label-title-only, duplicate-id-aria, color-contrast), so await render flushed and axe audited the real thing. color-contrast is the notable one — it is inert under jsdom and live in Chromium, so the port audits one rule more than the original could.

THE JSDOM TEST CLICKS AN ELEMENT NO USER COULD HIT. Both click tests in the original render a bare h(Label) with no slot, then call container.getElementsByTagName('label')[0].click(). An empty <label> is an inline box with no content: MEASURED at 0x18 in Chromium — zero WIDTH, full line-height — and Playwright refuses to click a zero-size element, so locator.click() retries and times out (probed with an explicit 1500ms timeout). jsdom does not care, because HTMLElement.click() dispatches on any node regardless of layout, and jsdom has no layout to consult. The port therefore gives both labels a text slot the original does not have. That is a deviation from the original body, recorded here rather than buried: it is forced by the environment, it cannot affect what is under test (the input is a SIBLING, not nested, so label text cannot create an implicit association), and it makes the test describe a gesture a user can actually perform. THE ASSERTIONS ARE UNCHANGED AND ARE NOT VACUOUS — verified by probing the positive case: the same real click on a label whose "for" DOES match focuses the input, so these two tests discriminate rather than passing because nothing happened. GENERALISES: any jsdom test that clicks an element with no intrinsic size is asserting about a gesture that cannot occur, and browser mode turns that from a silent pass into a timeout.

THE GAINED LINE, AND THE ENVIRONMENT EARNED IT — checked per PORTING.md 2.2 rather than assumed. The one line the port covers and jsdom does not is Label.vue:24, the inline @mousedown handler, which is the component's ONLY behaviour beyond rendering a <label> (it prevents text selection on double click). HTMLElement.click() — what the original calls, and what VTU's trigger('click') does too — dispatches a click event and NOTHING ELSE: no pointerdown, no mousedown, no focus, no mouseup. A real Playwright click dispatches the full sequence, so the handler runs. This is not a harness artifact of the kind #auto-unmount warns about: a jsdom test written this way cannot reach that line in ANY environment, and the coverage oracle proves it — the jsdom run performed the identical gesture on the identical element and reported the line uncovered. GENERALISES HARD, and is the best reason found so far to port T2 files that look boring: every mousedown / pointerdown / focus handler in the library is invisible to a jsdom test that clicks. BUT THE GAIN STOPS SHORT OF THE LOGIC, which line counts hide. Reading the istanbul BRANCH map instead: L24 carries two statements (hit 2 and 0) and its if-branch is [0,2] — taken zero times. event.detail > 1 is never true because no test in EITHER suite double-clicks, so preventDefault never runs and the double-click prevention this component exists to provide is exercised by nobody. A covered line is not a tested behaviour. Deliberately not fixed: adding that test would be an INVENTED it, which port:parity rejects and rule 7 forbids.

A GAP IN THE ORIGINAL SUITE, CARRIED OVER VERBATIM. Label has exactly one job — associate a <label> with a control via "for" — and the file tests it only in the negative: "should not focus the input when click on the label without a for attribute" and "...with a for attribute that does not match any input". Neither suite has a test that clicking a label whose "for" DOES match focuses the input, so both negatives would pass against a component that did nothing whatsoever. Confirmed live while validating the port (probe: real click on a matching label, document.activeElement becomes the INPUT), so the behaviour works and is simply unasserted. Left alone deliberately: a new it() is an INVENTED test that port:parity fails and rule 7 forbids, so the deliverable is this row rather than a patch. Worth noting the gap is not really the library's — "for" association is browser behaviour and this component only has to avoid breaking it — which is precisely the class of thing a jsdom suite cannot meaningfully assert and a browser suite can.

PORTED, 1/1 test, 2/2 assertions; port:checklist --complete, port:parity --complete and port:coverage all clean first try; jsdom original still green. The whole original file is one top-level it() with no describe, mounting the RAW PRIMITIVE (not the story fixture) twice — default then orientation:vertical — and running axe on each. No stubs installed, so none deleted. COVERAGE IS IDENTICAL: 35 lines in both, 0 lost and 0 GAINED, which is unusual (Label and useForwardExpose each gained one) and has a cause — Separator/BaseSeparator/Primitive have no teardown code, so the free unmount described in #auto-unmount reaches nothing new, and neither suite ever clicks or focuses, so #click-fires-no-mousedown does not apply either. THE ONE MECHANICAL THING THIS FILE TEACHES: two render() calls inside a SINGLE test behave sanely and the original ports literally. vitest-browser-vue registers cleanup in a beforeEach, not between renders, so the second render does NOT unmount the first — each call appends its own container to document.body and both stay mounted for the remainder of the test (probed: document.body.children.length === 2, both elements still connected), then both are removed before the next test (probed: 0 children; cleanup iterates a mountedWrappers Set, pure-*.js). The value of this port is jsdom removal, not new signal — see the two rows below for what the port actually surfaced, both of which are about axe rather than about Separator.

THIS COMPONENT ONLY TEST ASSERTS ALMOST NOTHING, IN BOTH ENVIRONMENTS, AND THE PORT DID NOT CHANGE THAT. Probed results.passes / results.violations / results.inapplicable per PORT-PROMPTS vacuity check. Chromium, horizontal mount (
): 5 rules pass — aria-allowed-role, aria-deprecated-role, aria-required-attr, aria-roles, nested-interactive — and 81 are inapplicable. Every one of those 5 is a check that the STRING "separator" is a real, non-deprecated role legal on a div; none of them checks that the separator is exposed at all. Vertical mount runs 10, the extra 5 (aria-allowed-attr, aria-conditional-attr, aria-prohibited-attr, aria-valid-attr, aria-valid-attr-value) applying only because aria-orientation="vertical" exists — so the SECOND mount is the only half of this test carrying weight, and the first is nearly free. DISCRIMINATION MEASURED, three mutations, identical verdicts in jsdom and Chromium: a misspelt role (role="seperator") IS caught (aria-roles), an invalid value (aria-orientation="sideways") IS caught (aria-valid-attr-value), but DELETING role ENTIRELY produces zero violations AND zero passes — a bare
is perfectly accessible — so the test cannot fail for the single most obvious way this component could break, namely not rendering its semantics. It also cannot fail for a wrong-but-valid orientation. Note this is the exact opposite of the Slider axe finding: nothing here was hidden by an unflushed mount (await render flushes, and the element is audited live), the rules genuinely have nothing to bite on. WHAT BROWSER MODE BOUGHT: nothing measurable. color-contrast, the rule that is inert under jsdom and live in Chromium (see Label row), is INAPPLICABLE here — the separator is headless, ships no styles, has no text and measures 414x0 in Chromium, so there is no contrast to compute. Recorded, not fixed: a stronger test would be an INVENTED it() and rule 7 forbids the patch.

GENERALISES TO EVERY AXE FILE IN THE REPO (62 of 97), AND WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL A PORT MADE THE TWO RUNS COMPARABLE. vitest-axe mount() branches on whether the node is already in the document (dist/index.js: `if (document.body.contains(html)) return [html, noop]; html = html.outerHTML` then `document.body.innerHTML = html` and audit document.body — the browser shim in shims/vitest-axe/index.ts reproduces this faithfully, checked line by line). VTU mount() leaves the component DETACHED, so every jsdom axe test in this repo takes the second branch: axe never sees the live component. It sees a COPY re-parsed from outerHTML, pasted into document.body, and the audit CONTEXT is document.body rather than the component. vitest-browser-vue render() attaches, so the browser port takes the first branch and audits the real element in place. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE on this file: jsdom reports 6 passing rules to the browser 5, the extra one being aria-hidden-body — a rule about <body aria-hidden>, i.e. about the harness page, that is only applicable because jsdom accidentally widened the context. So the port audits one rule fewer and loses nothing that concerns the component; the narrower context is the more faithful audit, not a weakening. TWO REASONS TO CARE BEYOND THE RULE COUNT. (1) An HTML round-trip drops everything not serialisable into attributes — live JS state, and any style not reachable from a global stylesheet — so a jsdom axe assertion is made against a static snapshot of markup, which is a fair description of what jsdom can check at all. (2) On any component big enough to hold landmarks or headings, the document.body context pulls in PAGE-level rules (region is already globally disabled in vitest.setup.ts for exactly this reason) and the jsdom and browser results will diverge in rule COUNT even when both are green. Expect this on the remaining 61 files; it is a property of the harness, not of the component under test.

3/3 tests, 5/3 assertions; port:checklist --complete, port:parity --complete and port:coverage all clean first try. A genuinely empty port: the original installs no stubs, so nothing was deleted, and coverage is identical line-for-line (83 lines both sides, 0 lost, 0 gained across 17 instrumented files). Note the zero GAIN despite vitest-browser-vue auto-unmounting every test (cf. shared/useForwardExpose.test.ts#auto-unmount): ProgressRoot/ProgressIndicator have no teardown code, so the free unmount buys nothing here. Cost, steady state over 3 runs each: 1.46s -> 2.17s wall clock (1.5x), vitest Duration 0.88s -> 1.57s (1.8x); test execution is unchanged (~250ms) because both are dominated by the fixture's 200ms setTimeout. No flake over 3 runs. The value of this port is not in the diff, it is in the two probes below.

Probed results.inapplicable/passes on BOTH sides per the Slider lesson, and the answer is the opposite of Slider: the jsdom axe test here is NOT vacuous. mount() renders synchronously and nothing in Progress is display:none, so aria-progressbar-name, aria-valid-attr-value, aria-allowed-attr, aria-required-attr and nested-interactive all run and pass under jsdom (13 passes / 0 violations / 73 inapplicable). The browser run is 12 passes / 0 violations. The ONE rule the browser adds is color-contrast, which is inapplicable under jsdom because it needs real computed colours and real compositing. It is not a formality: axe resolved fgColor #4ade80 (text-green-400) against a composited bgColor #4d4d4d (blackA9 over the white body) and scored 4.85:1 against a 4.5:1 threshold for 12px bold. A near miss. Any darkening of the fixture, any change to blackA9, and _Progress.vue starts failing its own accessibility test - and only the browser project would ever notice. Generalisable: for a static, always-visible component the axe port buys exactly one rule, but it is the rule jsdom structurally cannot run.

ProgressRoot has three progressState values (indeterminate / loading / complete). The jsdom suite and therefore the port only ever exercise loading, because the story fixture hardcodes 0 -> 50. That gap is exactly where the axe test would have failed. Probed (throwaway browser test, deleted): rendering ProgressRoot with modelValue=null emits <div aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuemin="0" role="progressbar" data-state="indeterminate" data-max="100"> - no aria-valuenow and NO aria-label, because the default getValueLabel returns undefined for a non-number. axe reports a real violation: aria-progressbar-name, 1 node. Inverted, this says the determinate axe test is close to unfailable: aria-progressbar-name can only pass because reka auto-names the progressbar with its own VALUE ("0%"), a name that describes nothing and changes as the bar fills. No test added - PORTING.md rule 7, an invented it fails port:parity. The fix belongs in ProgressRoot.vue (fall back to a real label, or drop role=progressbar when unnamed) and/or in _Progress.vue.

Translation-table hazard, generalisable. AGENTS.md says to prefer an awaited expect.element over a sync .element() read because it retries. For a test whose subject IS timing that retry is a silent weakening: describe("after 200ms") + await expect.element(...).toHaveAttribute("data-value","50") passes anywhere inside sleep(200) PLUS the ~1s retry budget, so it would stay green if the fixture flipped at 900ms. jsdom's expect(wrapper.html()).toContain(...) is a single instantaneous read and would not. Resolved by asserting twice - the retrying expect.element first (settles Vue's flush, no race), then the original's exact outerHTML toContain (no retry window, so the timing claim survives). Also worth recording why no race exists at all here: the fixture registers its setTimeout(200) inside its own setup(), i.e. strictly before await render() resolves and before the test's sleep(200) starts, so its callback fires first and Vue's microtask flush drains before the sleep's macrotask. Verified stable over 3 runs. Rule of thumb: when the describe name mentions a duration, do not let a retrying matcher be the only assertion.

AXE VACUITY CHECK, both environments MEASURED rather than reasoned about, and this file is the clean control case: neither suite's axe test is vacuous, and the jsdom/Chromium delta is EXACTLY ONE RULE. Census over the same story fixture — jsdom: 15 passing rules, 0 violations, 70 inapplicable, and color-contrast sitting in INCOMPLETE WITH ZERO NODES. Chromium: 16 passing, 0 violations, 70 inapplicable, and color-contrast PASSING WITH 2 NODES. Rule sets are otherwise identical, name for name. jsdom is not skipping the rule out of laziness — axe cannot compute a contrast ratio with no layout and no resolved colours, so it reports the rule as attempted-and-abandoned; the 0-node incomplete entry is the tell, and it is easy to misread as "ran and found nothing". The 2 Chromium nodes are the only text in the fixture: the ToolbarLink ("Edited 2 hours ago", mauve11 on white) and the Share ToolbarButton (white on violet9). The other 6 buttons hold @iconify/vue <Icon> glyphs and no text, so there is nothing to contrast. That is the concrete payoff of keeping colours in tailwind.browser.config.js, and it is honestly small: 2 nodes on a 7-button toolbar, both passing. UNLIKE Slider#axe, NOTHING WAS HIDDEN BY AN UNFLUSHED MOUNT — probed the jsdom original's [role=toolbar] tabindex at axe time and it is already "0", i.e. VTU had flushed and the live component really was audited. The rules doing actual work in both environments, and which would catch a regression: button-name (7 nodes, one per toggle item's aria-label), link-name (1), aria-hidden-focus (6), nested-interactive (9), tabindex (9), aria-allowed-role (11). ALSO MEASURED WHILE IN THERE: every button is 0x0 under jsdom and 23x25 in Chromium (toolbar root 414x45). That is both the mechanical reason color-contrast cannot run under jsdom and a standing reminder that any future click test on this fixture works only because the CSS shim exists.

THE COMPONENT'S DEFINING BEHAVIOUR IS TESTED BY NEITHER SUITE, AND THE PORT IS FORBIDDEN TO FIX IT. ToolbarRoot IS a RovingFocusGroup (ToolbarRoot.vue:41) — arrow-key navigation across a single tab stop is the whole reason Toolbar exists as a primitive rather than a styled div. Toolbar.test.ts asserts only that the roving group's tabindex flips between "0" and "-1", and declines the rest in a source comment: "Since Toolbar is just a collection of ToggleGroup, so would exclude the test here". Neither file dispatches a key, a click or a focus event. VERIFIED FROM THE ISTANBUL LINE MAP of the browser run, not inferred from reading: RovingFocusGroup.vue handleFocus (L90-121 — the ENTRY_FOCUS dispatch and the candidate-item selection that decides WHICH item receives focus on entry) is entirely uncovered; so is RovingFocusItem.vue L50-96, the entire keydown/focus block; so is RovingFocus/utils.ts focusFirst (L37-53). The tab stop those two tabbable tests assert is one that no test ever tabs to. THIS IS THE FILE WHERE BROWSER MODE WOULD HAVE PAID MOST AND WAS HANDED NOTHING TO DO. Keyboard roving focus is precisely the class of behaviour jsdom fakes badly — jsdom fires keydown at whatever element you name it at, so a single-tab-stop widget can be "tested" without focus ever being where the user's focus would be, while Playwright routes the key to document.activeElement and the test either focuses the right element or fails. The port inherits an empty slot instead. Recorded rather than patched: a new it() is an INVENTED test, which port:parity rejects and rule 7 forbids. If PORTING.md Phase 3's per-component deletion decision reopens this file, arrow-key navigation is the test to add, and it should be added to the BROWSER file only.

5/5 tests, 9/9 assertions, all four oracles clean on the first run; 0 lines gained, 0 lost, 10 files instrumented on both sides. No stubs to delete - the original installs none. The result worth having is that this file is NOT the mechanical port the translation table produces: two of its rules are actively wrong here and both were settled by measurement, see #render-rejects-attachTo and #body-reset-required. The counts were confirmed to discriminate rather than pass trivially - nothing mounted gives 0, one component gives 2, unmounted gives 0, and with two components the reading after wrapper1.unmount() is still 2, so the module-level refcount in useFocusGuards.ts is genuinely exercised. Two render() calls in one test do not unmount each other (cleanup is a root-suite beforeEach, not per-render) so both refcount tests port literally. The #auto-unmount coverage freebie explicitly does NOT apply: the original calls wrapper.unmount() in all five tests, which is also why nothing was gained. The original comment watchEffect runs synchronously on mount survives the await - measured, the count is already 2 on a synchronous read taken before awaiting render() at all, and markThenable only awaits a trace mark rather than a Vue flush, and expect(countGuards()) is a plain non-retrying assertion in both suites so no retry budget widened anything. 5/5 tests, 6/6 assertions; port:checklist --complete, port:parity --complete and port:coverage all clean (14 files instrumented on both sides, 50 shared lines, 0 lost 0 gained). One test quarantined — see #nonce-attribute. No stubs to delete: the original installs none. The notable mechanical fact is that NOTHING in this component is reachable by a locator — the root is a fragment of <div data-reka-viewport role="presentation"> plus a sibling <style>; "presentation" is not a queryable role and <style> has no role and no accessible text, so getByRole even with includeHidden cannot address either. screen.container.querySelector is the faithful translation of wrapper.find(selector) here rather than a contortion; both roots are direct children of container (measured: ['DIV','STYLE']). The original beforeEach(() => document.body.innerHTML = '') was already dead code under jsdom — every test mounts with attachTo: document.body and calls wrapper.unmount() itself — and is deleted. QUARANTINED via it.fails, assertion unchanged. The original asserts styleEl.attributes('nonce') === 'abc123' under a comment saying jsdom exposes the attribute reliably; that comment describes a jsdom implementation detail as if it were platform behaviour. Measured, same component, nonce prop abc123, style element connected to the document in both cases: jsdom getAttribute=abc123 hasAttribute=true el.nonce=abc123; Chromium getAttribute=null hasAttribute=false el.nonce=abc123. It is NOT the HTML spec nonce-hiding behaviour, which was the standing prediction — hiding empties the content attribute but leaves it present, and only fires for a header-delivered CSP. Probed directly on the vitest page: setAttribute nonce then insert leaves hasAttribute true, so no hiding occurred. The actual cause is Vue: shouldSetAsProp in @vue/runtime-dom patchProp ends in "return key in el", nonce is in HTMLStyleElement in BOTH environments, so Vue assigns el.nonce as a DOM property and never calls setAttribute — jsdom reflects that IDL setter into the content attribute, Chromium writes only the internal nonce slot. Consumer impact: (b) test artifact, not a real problem. Probed in an iframe under meta CSP style-src nonce-abc123 — a style element whose nonce was set via the IDL property before insertion APPLIES (computed rgb(1,2,3)), identically to one set via setAttribute (rgb(4,5,6)), while a nonce-less style is BLOCKED (rgb(0,0,0)). Vue patches props before hostInsert, so the nonce is in place when CSP evaluates the element, and SSR still emits nonce= as a real attribute. The only real consequence is that client-rendered DOM has no [nonce] attribute to grep for. Fixing the test means asserting el.nonce, which is a change of what is checked and collides with the verbatim-name rule, so it is left quarantined rather than silently switched.

The test named "renders a <style> sibling whose text mentions [data-reka-viewport]" cannot fail for the reason it exists. Mutation-verified in the browser project: renaming the div attribute to data-reka-viewport-MUTATED and role to none turns the other three tests red and leaves this one GREEN, because it compares a string literal in the component template against a string literal in the test. Nothing in either suite ties the injected stylesheet selector to the element it is meant to select, and nothing asserts the sheet has any effect at all. Checked whether browser mode could add that: it cannot claim it as a win, because both environments already apply the sheet — getComputedStyle(viewport).scrollbarWidth is none and styleEl.sheet.cssRules.length is 2 in Chromium AND in jsdom (which runs with resources: usable). So this is a gap in the original suite, not a jsdom limitation. An it asserting the computed scrollbar-width would be INVENTED under rule 7, hence found-gap rather than a patch.

applies overflow:auto style reads el.style.overflow — the inline property the component wrote, not what the browser resolved — so it is byte-identical in jsdom and Chromium and the port gains nothing by being in a browser. Ported verbatim; checked whether the browser could say more and it cannot: getComputedStyle(el).overflow is auto in both. What no test in either suite touches is the rest of the same style binding. Viewport.vue carries a three-line comment explaining that position: relative is load-bearing so that selectedItem.offsetTop is measured relative to the viewport rather than the scrollUpButton, and sets flex: 1 beside it; neither value is asserted anywhere, and the behaviour the comment is about — that offsetTop actually resolves against this element, and that the viewport actually scrolls — is only observable in a real browser and is observed by nobody. This is the one place on this file where browser mode could buy something real, and rule 7 forbids the added it.

TRANSLATION-TABLE CORRECTION, verified in source and by running it. AGENTS.md states that vitest-browser-vue render accepts all @vue/test-utils mount options, so most of this is mechanical. It does not accept attachTo: dist/pure-epEwB8Ps.js throws outright - if (mountOptions.attachTo) throw new Error(attachTo is not supported, use container instead). render owns the mount point, appending its own container div to baseElement (document.body by default), passing attachTo: container to VTU itself and then unwrapping VTU intermediate node. All five tests in this file pass attachTo: document.body, so a literal application of the table crashes the entire file before a single assertion runs. The correct replacement is to DROP the option, not to pass container: document.body - the component still lands inside the live document, one div deeper, which is all these tests need because useFocusGuards inserts its guards relative to document.body rather than relative to the component. Measured body layout after one render: span[guard], div[container], span[guard]. This will hit every ported file that mounts with attachTo, not just this one.

THE AGENTS.md RULE beforeEach(document.body.innerHTML = ) -> DELETE IS WRONG FOR THIS FILE, and the failure it causes is silent. Every assertion here is a document.querySelectorAll([data-reka-focus-guard]) count over the WHOLE document, so one leaked node turns expect(countGuards()).toBe(2) into a test that passes for the wrong reason. The table justification - render removes its container - is only true for containers cleanup() unmounts itself: cleanup() removes a container only when wrapper.element.parentNode.parentNode === document.body, and every test here calls unmount() explicitly first, so the emptied container divs accumulate. Measured: __vitest_1__, __vitest_2__ and __vitest_3__ were all still in body at the fourth test. Keeping the reset is also SAFE, which had to be checked separately rather than assumed, since clearing body could plausibly destroy runner scaffolding or a container render is about to use. Two measurements say it does not: the tester iframe body holds nothing but render containers (empty at the first beforeEach, no runner elements), and vitest-browser-vue registers beforeEach(cleanup) on the FILE ROOT suite while this reset lives inside a describe, so vitest parent-first hook ordering guarantees cleanup() runs first and never finds its DOM yanked out from under it. Verified with a deliberately leaked mount: the next test still started at 0 guards and still counted 2 then 0 around a fresh render, so useFocusGuards module-level refcount did not desync either. General rule for the guide: delete the body reset when the assertions are container-scoped, KEEP it when they are document-scoped.

WHAT THE COMPONENT EXISTS FOR IS TESTED BY NEITHER SUITE, AND ONLY THE BROWSER COULD TEST IT. useFocusGuards injects a pair of tabindex=0 sentinel spans at the very start and very end of document.body so that focus leaving a modal fires a catchable focusin/focusout instead of escaping to the browser chrome. Both files only ever COUNT those spans; neither presses Tab. Measured in Chromium with a throwaway probe (deleted): with two buttons rendered inside FocusGuards, Tab from the last button lands on the TRAILING guard, a second Tab leaves to BODY, and Shift+Tab from the first button lands on the LEADING guard - the guards really are in the sequential focus order and the mechanism works. Notable against the AGENTS.md zero-size gotcha: the guards measure EXACTLY 0x0 (position:fixed, opacity:0, pointer-events:none) and Chromium tabs to them regardless, so being zero-size blocks locator.click() but NOT sequential focus navigation. jsdom is structurally incapable of this test, which is the whole point - measured in the unit project, dispatching a Tab keydown at the focused button leaves document.activeElement unchanged, because jsdom implements no sequential focus navigation at all; only programmatic .focus() moves focus there, and that works identically in both environments so it proves nothing about the guards. The port cannot close this gap: an added it would be reported as INVENTED by port:parity and rule 7 forbids touching source. It is the strongest candidate in this file for a test worth writing once new tests are permitted.

NEGATIVE RESULT, recorded because it was predicted to be positive. Neither file has an axe test, so any violation would have had to be filed here rather than quarantined; the prediction was that two empty focusable tabindex=0 spans with no accessible name would trip aria-hidden-focus or focus-order-semantics. Measured in Chromium (throwaway probe, deleted) running axe over document.body with FocusGuards wrapped around a main/h1/button: 0 violations, 10 passing rules, 0 incomplete, 76 inapplicable. The tabindex rule PASSES with 2 nodes, i.e. it examined both guards and accepted them, because it only rejects tabindex greater than 0. aria-hidden-focus is INAPPLICABLE - the guards are not aria-hidden, so the rule has nothing to match. Worth writing down that axe silence is not a clean bill of health here: the guards are real unnamed tab stops for a keyboard or screen-reader user and no axe rule covers focusable element with no accessible name and no role. That is upstream Radix behaviour and a deliberate tradeoff, not a reka regression, so there is nothing to file against the component - but it does mean an axe test added to this file in future would be near-vacuous with respect to the guards themselves, the same shape as Separator#axe-near-vacuous.

PORTED, 9/9 tests, 10/10 assertions; port:checklist --complete, port:parity --complete and port:coverage all clean on the FIRST run, jsdom original still 9/9 green. No stubs to delete (the original installs none) and NO #auto-unmount freebie either: the original already calls wrapper.unmount() after all nine of its mounts and uses attachTo: document.body, so the browser is owed no teardown lines — coverage came out +0/-0 over 12 instrumented files / 23 shared lines. Three deletions only: attachTo, unmount, and the two beforeEach(() => document.body.innerHTML = '') hooks; the last verified redundant rather than assumed (probed: document.body holds ZERO children at the start of every test and one after render). The port is faithful and boring. Everything worth knowing about this file is in the three rows below, and none of it is about the port being wrong.

THE ONE TEST ABOUT THE COMPONENT'S ACTUAL JOB CANNOT FAIL, AND THE PORT DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX IT. "applies visually-hidden styles" asserts el.style.position === "absolute" and el.style.clipPath === "inset(50%)" — the inline string the component WROTE, not what the browser DID with it. jsdom structurally cannot do better; Chromium can, and the port still reads inline style, because asserting computed values would close the gap rather than record it and an added it() would be INVENTED (rule 7 / port:parity). Demonstrated, not argued: apply a class of !important overrides (position:static, clip-path:none, width/height:auto, margin:0, overflow:visible) to the same component and BOTH original assertions still PASS — inline position "absolute", clipPath "inset(50%)" — while getComputedStyle reports position "static" / clip-path "none", the element measures 122.27x18, and document.elementFromPoint at its centre returns the element itself. Fully visible, fully clickable, test green. What the component actually does when nothing fights it, measured in Chromium: computed position absolute, clip-path inset(50%), clip rect(0px 0px 0px 0px), overflow hidden, a 1x1 box at (-2,-2) (top/left -1px plus margin -1px), scrollWidth 122 (the text is laid out, then clipped), and elementFromPoint at its centre returns null. So the component genuinely does hide content — and neither suite asserts one word of it. One negative result worth reusing: el.checkVisibility({checkOpacity,checkVisibilityCSS}) returns TRUE for a correctly hidden element, because Chromium ignores clip-path and 1px geometry, so it is NOT a usable oracle for "visually hidden". Use getBoundingClientRect plus elementFromPoint.

THE COMPONENT NEVER LEAVES ITS CONTENT IN THE ACCESSIBILITY TREE — IN EITHER MODE — AND THE SUITE PINS THAT AS IF IT WERE CORRECT. VisuallyHidden.vue:19 reads :aria-hidden="feature === 'focusable' || feature === 'fully-hidden' ? 'true' : undefined" and feature is typed 'focusable' | 'fully-hidden', so the expression is unconditionally "true". Measured in Chromium with two independent accessible-name implementations, which agree: <button><VisuallyHidden>Save</VisuallyHidden></button> produces an axe button-name VIOLATION for both features, and page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }) matches 0 elements (1 with includeHidden); an identical span with identical CSS but no aria-hidden PASSES button-name and matches 1. <label><VisuallyHidden>Search query</VisuallyHidden></label> + <input id> is an axe "label" violation. The path that still works is a DIRECT aria-labelledby/aria-describedby IDREF — the accname spec exempts directly-referenced hidden nodes — probed: button-name passes, locator matches 1. That is how Tooltip/TooltipContentImpl.vue uses it, so the library's own usage is mostly fine; what silently disappears is sr-only text NESTED inside a control, i.e. the canonical use of a component called VisuallyHidden. The jsdom suite asserts aria-hidden="true" under 'given feature="focusable" (default)' with no comment at all. Not a fork artifact: upstream reka-ui v2 is byte-identical, and git blame splits the expression — the "|| feature === 'fully-hidden'" half arrived in 1460e5aa (a deliberate fix), the 'focusable' half predates it. Recorded only; rule 7 forbids the patch and an added test would be INVENTED.

THE SOURCE COMMENT'S SAFETY CLAIM IS TRUE FOR fully-hidden AND FALSE FOR THE OTHER MODE, AND NEITHER SUITE CAN NOTICE BECAUSE THIS FILE HAS NO AXE TEST AT ALL. The comment inside 'sets aria-hidden="true"' (fully-hidden) argues tabindex="-1" makes aria-hidden safe, i.e. no aria-hidden-focus risk. Verified in Chromium rather than trusted: axe over a fully-hidden VisuallyHidden reports 0 violations and lists aria-hidden-focus in PASSES. But aria-hidden is set for 'focusable' too (see #not-in-a11y-tree), and Toast/FocusProxy.vue renders <VisuallyHidden tabindex="0" style="position: fixed" @focus=...>. Probed that exact shape: axe reports aria-hidden-focus, impact SERIOUS, 1 node, and el.focus() succeeds (document.activeElement === el) — a keyboard-reachable element removed from the accessibility tree, which is the precise thing the rule exists for. The prop is literally named "focusable" and its mode is the one that makes focusable content a violation. Out of scope to fix or to test here (Toast has its own file); recorded because this file's assertions are what pin the attribute in place.

THE OPEN DIALOG HAS A REAL COLOUR-CONTRAST VIOLATION AND jsdom CANNOT SEE IT. Quarantined under it.fails with the assertion unchanged. axe over document.body after opening reports color-contrast, 1 node: the fixture action button (text-red11 on bg-red4) computes #ce2c31 on #ffdbdc = 4.07:1 against the 4.5:1 threshold at 16px/normal. Not a shim artifact - tailwind.browser.config.js carries the same @radix-ui/colors palette as .histoire/tailwind.config.js verbatim (diffed), so this is what a Histoire viewer sees. Lives in story/_AlertDialog.vue, i.e. fixture styling, not library code, so rule 7 applies: reported not patched. Same shape as the Slider axe row but arrived at differently - the jsdom original here is NOT vacuous (see #axe-census), it simply runs a rule set that structurally excludes contrast.

PORTED, 4/4 tests, 7/6 assertions; port:checklist --complete and port:parity --complete clean, jsdom original still 4/4 green. 1 test quarantined (#axe-color-contrast). No stubs to delete - the original installs none. THE ONE TRANSLATION THAT IS NOT IN THE TABLE AND WOULD SILENTLY BREAK A PORT: AlertDialogPortal TELEPORTS the content to document.body, so once the dialog is open NOTHING under test is inside screen.container. screen.getBy* is container-scoped and finds zero; the document-scoped root is `page` from vitest/browser, which is the direct equivalent of @testing-library/vue findByRole(document.body, ...). Every portalled component (Dialog, Popover, Select, Tooltip, Toast, DropdownMenu...) will hit this. Second measured note, from the mutation runs: the retrying `expect.element(...).toHaveFocus()` that settles AlertDialogContent nextTick focus turns a failing focus assertion from 8ms under jsdom into a 15009ms locator timeout in the browser - correct, but a mutation/regression loop on a focus-heavy file is ~2000x slower to go red. Coverage: +1 (DialogContentImpl.vue:63), -6 all argued per line in PORT-COVERAGE-ALLOW.tsv (#scrollbar-width-jsdom, #focus-scope-pause-leak). Mutation-verified per PORTING.md 2.3 even though this is T2: role="alertdialog" -> role="dialog" and neutering the cancel-button auto-focus each turn exactly one test red in BOTH suites, so these three tests are real, not decorative.

NEGATIVE RESULT on vacuity, recorded because the Slider precedent predicts the opposite. The jsdom axe test here is NOT vacuous: with the dialog open it reports 17 passing rules over real nodes (aria-dialog-name 1, button-name 4, nested-interactive 4, tabindex 1, duplicate-id-aria 3, heading-order 1) and 0 violations, so it genuinely audits the open dialog. Slider was vacuous for a reason that does not apply here - an element display:none at mount time - and mount() renders this fixture synchronously with nothing hidden. What Chromium adds is exactly two rules that have nodes to examine: color-contrast (5 passes + 1 violation, see #axe-color-contrast) and avoid-inline-spacing (3 passes). Everything else is identical. ONE CORRECTION TO THE AGENTS.md CENSUS ADVICE, measured here: "under jsdom color-contrast lands in incomplete with zero nodes" is only half right - in the SAME test file, the same rule landed in `incomplete` (0 nodes) on the closed dialog and in `inapplicable` (0 nodes) on the open one. The bucket is not stable, so a census must treat zero-node entries in BOTH incomplete and inapplicable as "did not run"; counting buckets is not enough, you have to read the node counts.

jsdom COVERS THE SCROLLBAR-COMPENSATION BRANCH BY COMPUTING A NONSENSE VALUE, AND NO TEST CHECKS THE VALUE. useBodyScrollLock.ts:60 does `window.innerWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth`, then L72 gates L73-76 on that being > 0. Measured: jsdom reports innerWidth 1024 and documentElement.clientWidth 0 (it does no layout, so clientWidth is always 0), giving a 1024px "scrollbar", so opening any modal under jsdom sets document.body.style.paddingRight = "1024px" and --scrollbar-width: 1024px. In the Chromium tester iframe the same read is 414 - 414 = 0, the branch is correctly skipped, and body overflow:hidden still lands via the nextTick path at L93 - i.e. the port loses the four LINES and loses nothing about the behaviour. jsdom reached them on a SINGLE test, so this is not a multi-test artifact. The gap: no test in either suite asserts paddingRight/marginRight/--scrollbar-width at all, so jsdom "covered" four lines while they produced an absurd value and nothing noticed. Honest caveat - this is a property of the tester iframe (no scrollbar present), not of browser mode: a browser page that DOES overflow would take the branch, and testing it properly needs a fixture tall enough to scroll. Allowed per line in PORT-COVERAGE-ALLOW.tsv.

THE ONLY jsdom COVERAGE OF FocusScope pause()/resume() IS TEST-TO-TEST BLEED, NOT A TEST. FocusScope.vue:81 (pause) and :84 (resume) fire only when TWO focus scopes are on the shared module-level stack at once (FocusScope/stack.ts add/remove). No test in this file ever opens two dialogs. Measured by bisecting the coverage run: with ONE jsdom test selected (-t "should open the content") L81/L84 are NOT covered; with TWO (-t "content") they are. The browser port does not cover them with any number of tests. Mechanism: FocusScope.vue:251 defers focusScopesStack.remove(focusScope) inside setTimeout(..., 0) in the watchEffect cleanup, so under jsdom the previous test unmount has not yet dropped its scope when the next test mount calls add() - activeFocusScope.pause() fires, and the stale timer then finds a survivor and calls resume(). The awaited render+click in the browser port spans enough macrotasks that the stale scope is gone first. So the port losing these two lines is the port being CLEANER, and the real result is that scope stacking - the thing that stops a nested Dialog from breaking its parent trap - is exercised by neither suite on purpose. Allowed per line in PORT-COVERAGE-ALLOW.tsv.

THE TWO THINGS AN ALERT DIALOG IS FOR - TRAPPING FOCUS AND CLOSING ON ESCAPE - ARE TESTED BY NEITHER SUITE, AND ONE OF THEM ONLY THE BROWSER CAN TEST. Neither AlertDialog.test.ts nor the port contains the string Tab or Escape. Confirmed from the istanbul line map rather than by reading: with the whole file run, DismissableLayer.vue L149-156 (the Escape handler body: present check, isHighestLayer, emit escapeKeyDown, emit dismiss) has ZERO hits in BOTH projects - only L144, the onKeyStroke registration, is covered - and FocusScope.vue handleKeyDown L271-296 (the entire Tab-wrap block) and the focus trap-back branches L101 (focusin) and L125 (focusout) are unreached in both. A throwaway browser probe (deleted) pressing {Tab} and {Escape} once reaches 15 FocusScope lines, 6 DismissableLayer lines and DialogContentImpl L99-100 that no test in either suite touches. What the probe showed the untested code actually does, in Chromium: Tab from the auto-focused Cancel button cycles Cancel -> "Yes, delete account" -> "hihi" -> Cancel and never leaves the dialog, Shift+Tab wraps backwards, and Escape closes the dialog, restores body pointer-events to "" and returns focus to the trigger. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY, worth stating because it is easy to over-claim: the TAB half is jsdom-unportable in the AGENTS.md sense - the same probe under jsdom leaves document.activeElement on Cancel after three Tab keydowns, because jsdom has no sequential focus navigation - but the ESCAPE half is NOT: fireEvent.keyDown(document, {key: "Escape"}) under jsdom closes the dialog and restores focus to the trigger exactly as Chromium does. So Escape is a plain gap in the suite that jsdom could always have covered, and only the focus trap is a gap browser mode uniquely unlocks. Rule 7 forbids adding either test here (port:parity would report INVENTED); both are prime candidates once new tests are permitted.

THE ONE GAINED LINE, AND THE ENVIRONMENT EARNED IT, NOT THE HARNESS. DialogContentImpl.vue:63 - `rootContext.triggerElement.value = getActiveElement()`, guarded on L62 by `getActiveElement() !== document.body` and commented "Preserve the DialogTrigger element in case it was triggered programmatically" - is covered by the port and by no jsdom test. Cause measured directly rather than inferred: a probe (deleted) reading document.activeElement immediately after `wrapper.find("button").element.click()` under jsdom reports BODY both before and after, because HTMLElement.click() dispatches a click and nothing else, so the guard is false when DialogContentImpl mounts. Playwright focuses the button before clicking it, so the branch is taken. This is NOT the #auto-unmount freebie - adding wrapper.unmount() to the jsdom test would not reach it; you would have to add an explicit .focus() the original never had - so it belongs to the same family as Label#click-fires-no-mousedown and is a real point for browser mode. Caveat against over-claiming: focus still returns to the trigger after Escape under jsdom (probed), so the missed line does not visibly break the jsdom suite - it just means the branch that records the trigger was never executed there.

9/9 tests, 15/8 assertions; port:checklist --complete, port:parity --complete and port:coverage all clean on the first run. No stubs to delete - the original installs none. Zero coverage delta: both suites reach the same 102 lines across 22 instrumented files. Cost, steady state over 3 runs each: 1.19s -> 1.97s wall clock (1.65x), vitest Duration 690ms -> 1.43s, test execution 64ms -> 257ms (4x). Three additions that are neither weakenings nor decoration, each measured: a geometry <style> because the component is literally unclickable in Chromium (#zero-size-switch), { exact: true } on every getByText because the locator default is a substring match (#getbytext-substring), and an explicit expect around every bare getBy* that WAS the assertion in a @testing-library original (#lazy-locator-vacuum). Mutation-verified four ways (#mutation).

_Switch.vue styles nothing and SwitchRoot renders as a <button> containing an empty <span>, so in Chromium the switch measures EXACTLY 0x0 and Playwright will not click it; force: true fails too, with 'Element is outside of the viewport'. The cause is the CSS shim added in B3, not its absence: Tailwind preflight sets button{padding:0} and *{border-width:0}, which deletes the UA box an empty button would otherwise have. Measured against an identical empty <button> inside a shadow root, where preflight cannot reach - 16x6 there and computed padding 1px 6px / border 2px, versus 0x0 and 0/0 in the light DOM. Fixed test-file-locally: a <style> appended in beforeAll giving [data-testid=root] 40x24 and [data-testid=thumb] 16x16, removed in afterAll. Generalises: the shim that makes styled fixtures clickable makes UNSTYLED ones unclickable, so 'element is not visible' on a plain <button> is a shim symptom rather than a locator bug. Any fixture whose interactive element has no text and no size classes is a candidate - measure with getBoundingClientRect() before debugging the locator.

Vitest's locator getByText defaults to a SUBSTRING match where @testing-library's getByText defaults to whole-string. Measured on this fixture: screen.getByText('checked').elements() returns 1 element whose textContent is 'unchecked'; with { exact: true } it returns 0, and getByText('unchecked', { exact: true }) returns 1. So a literal port of the original's getByText('checked') / getByText('unchecked') toggle assertions matches the same

in both states, and both toggle tests would pass against a switch that never toggles. port:parity cannot see this - the assertion count is unchanged. Every getByText in the port carries { exact: true }. Sweep other ports for bare getByText, especially where the two expected strings are prefixes of one another (checked/unchecked, valid/invalid, enabled/disabled, selected/unselected).

@testing-library's getBy* throws when it misses, so a bare 'screen.getByTestId("thumb")' with no expect around it IS the assertion - three of the four tests in the first describe assert only that way, and 'thumb can render' contains no expect at all. A vitest locator is lazy and constructs happily against nothing: measured, screen.getByTestId('does-not-exist') and screen.getByText('definitely-not-here') both return without throwing. A mechanical line-for-line port of those tests is therefore a no-op, and port:parity scores it clean because 0 expects out of 0 expects is not a weakening. Rule: every bare getBy* inherited from a @testing-library original must become 'await expect.element(...).toBeInTheDocument()'. This is the mirror image of #getbytext-substring - both turn a green ported test into one that asserts nothing, and neither is visible to the oracle.

SwitchRoot.vue:117 is @keydown.enter.prevent="toggleCheck" on a real <button>, and the .prevent is load-bearing in exactly one environment. Under jsdom it is inert and untested: fireEvent.keyDown dispatches a keydown with no default action to cancel, so the handler is the only thing that runs and the test passes whether or not preventDefault is called. In Chromium, Enter on a <button> also synthesises a click, which reaches @click="toggleCheck" - so without preventDefault the switch toggles twice per Enter and lands back where it started. Mutation-verified: rewriting the binding as @keydown.enter turns the browser test 'keydown enter root will toggle value' RED and leaves the jsdom original GREEN. A one-token modifier guarding a real double-fire that the jsdom suite structurally cannot reach - the T3 payoff shape on a file tiered T2.

Four mutations, run in both projects, source reverted with the editor and confirmed clean with git diff --stat. (1) Delete @click="toggleCheck": browser 3 red, jsdom 2 red. The extra one is 'after uncheck and click submit button again' - under jsdom that test submits {} whether or not the toggle works, because a switch that cannot check also cannot be checked, so it CANNOT FAIL on a broken toggle. The port asserts aria-checked true then false in its beforeEach, so it does fail. (2) Rewrite @keydown.enter.prevent as @keydown.enter: browser 1 red, jsdom 0 red - see #enter-prevent-untested-in-jsdom. (3) Delete role="switch": browser 5 red, jsdom 2 red. Both catch it through axe (the orphaned aria-checked trips aria-allowed-attr); the port additionally catches it in every getByRole('switch') query, which is why it ports container.querySelector('button') to a role locator. (4) Move VisuallyHiddenInput inside the Primitive slot: 2 red on both sides, so 'should not nest the hidden input inside the interactive control' is discriminating in both environments and needed no help. Net: the port is strictly more sensitive on every mutation, and one original test is unfailable.

The jsdom axe test audits a DOM the component does not keep. useFormControl returns true while currentElement is still undefined (the deliberate SSR default), so the first synchronous render of a standalone Switch emits a VisuallyHiddenInput; mount() does not flush, so axe(wrapper.element) sees it.
